title: Split SRP (one hart): a link-up inside a loop pass resets the interface twice and loses the startup participants
body:
**Found by** the second-hart lane's harness differential (#872 issuecomment-7081009316, item 1). It applies to the **one-hart shipping image** (the split default after #960).

**Observed:**
- The loop reads the LINK register at the start of a pass. If the link comes up during that pass, SRP's poll reads the register later in the same pass.
- The poll then resets the interface on a level no LINK event has carried yet.
- The LINK dispatched on the next pass is a repeat, and resets the interface again.
- So SRP resets the interface twice at the link-up and reopens it, and loses the clean startup participants that a first UP keeps.

**Why the tests miss it:** in the one-hart CPU budget harness, `wait quiet` ends on the pass boundary, so the link always comes up as a pass starts. On hardware a link moves at any time.

**The two-hart fix to port:** on two harts, SRP's poll compares the level the loop dispatched (`ctrl_loop_link_up`) instead of the register (the second-hart lane's `8fc723ee`). A host test in its own process, `CrossApp.ALinkUpInsideHartZerosPassIsTheFirstUp`, raises the link between the loop's read and SRP's poll; a planted defect reverts the fix.

**Acceptance:**
- on the one-hart image, a link-up at any phase of a pass resets SRP's interface once, with the startup participants kept;
- the host test of that ordering fails before the fix and passes after, at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, with a planted defect;
- the CPU budget rows unchanged within their bounds;
- the images within their ledgers.

Relates to #665, #970, #972.
